details.description: Qwen3.8-27B is a dense 27-billion-parameter multimodal model from Alibaba's Qwen team, part of the Qwen3.8 series (built on the Qwen3.5 architecture) and released in August 2026. It combines text generation with native vision-language understanding of images and documents, and supports a toggleable "thinking" reasoning mode with an adjustable reasoning_effort parameter, plus tool calling for agentic use. Qwen's own model card states a native context length of 262,144 tokens, extensible to 1,000,000 tokens; on this catalog it is listed with a 131,042-token input limit and a 16,384-token output limit.
advantages: Scores 90.3% on LiveCodeBench v6 for competitive coding, per its Hugging Face model card.
Scores 89.2% on GPQA Diamond for scientific reasoning, per its Hugging Face model card.
Scores 84.3% on OSWorld-Verified for computer-use tasks and 81.9% on AndroidWorld for mobile-use tasks, per its Hugging Face model card.
Scores 91.1% on OmniDocBench 1.5 for document understanding, per its Hugging Face model card.
Supports a toggleable "thinking" reasoning mode with an adjustable reasoning_effort parameter and tool calling, per its Hugging Face model card and GitHub README.
disadvantages: Groq's model listing marks this model as a preview, "intended for evaluation purposes only and should not be used in production environments."
Released in August 2026, so it has limited independent evaluation beyond the maker's own benchmark tables.
use_cases: Long-horizon autonomous planning and computer-use agents (browser, desktop, mobile).
Visual math and scientific reasoning tasks.
General chat with an optional extended "thinking" mode for harder problems.

notes: Catalog's max_input_tokens (131,042) is well below the 262,144-token native context (extensible to 1,000,000 with RoPE/YaRN scaling) stated on Qwen's Hugging Face card; kept the catalog's value per instructions and noted the maker's figure in the description. Groq's own model page lists this id as a preview model not intended for production. The maker's model card did not state a specific list of supported languages, so languages is left empty. Qwen's Hugging Face card and GitHub README also describe native video understanding ("hour-scale videos"), but the catalog's modality facts list only image_input (no video); video was removed from the description and use cases so the write-up does not restate a modality the catalog does not have. Benchmark names OSWorld, WebArena and OmniDocBench were corrected to the exact table headings (OSWorld-Verified, WebArena-Verified, OmniDocBench 1.5) shown on the model card.
